key_insight: Adaptive syndrome extraction in surface-GKP codes can skip noisy measurements when reused syndromes are more reliable, cutting overhead without sacrificing logical performance.
engineering_relevance: This reduces stabilizer-measurement cost and ancilla demand in fault-tolerant quantum hardware, especially when measurement and gate noise dominate idle noise.
method: Use analog information from inner GKP correction to estimate syndrome reliability.
At each round, choose among four actions: measure both X/Z stabilizers, measure only one type, or skip both and reuse prior syndromes.
Base the decision on a comparison between the reliability of reused versus freshly measured syndromes.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations show the adaptive skipping scheme lowers stabilizer-measurement count while keeping logical error rates comparable to or better than a full-measurement baseline.
watch_item: The benefit depends on the hardware noise regime, so the policy may need retuning when idle noise is not smaller than gate/measurement noise.
paper_title: When to Skip Syndrome Extraction in Surface-GKP Codes
